strongest_angle: Researchers in southwestern Ethiopia rediscovered the amphibious Ethiopian water mouse (Nilopegamys plumbeus) nearly a century after its last recorded sighting in 1927, finding three specimens in the Yayu biosphere reserve.

key_facts.fact: The Ethiopian water mouse (Nilopegamys plumbeus) was rediscovered by a research team in southwestern Ethiopia, who found three animals in October 2026 whose features match the species description.
Prior to the rediscovery in southwestern Ethiopia, the amphibious rodent had not been recorded since 1927, leaving only a single museum specimen known for nearly a century.
The rediscovery of the rare mammalian genus Nilopegamys took place within the Yayu biosphere reserve located in southwestern Ethiopia by an Ethiopian-Czech research team.
The new sighting of Nilopegamys plumbeus occurred approximately 350 kilometers away from the original 1927 record location.
